verdicts.item: graph-theory: Hosoya Z wrong for every molecule with >18 bonds (also landscape-2026 and redteam-paper duplicates)
verdicts.reproduction: Read ml.py:115-140: m>25 returns 1+m+m(m-1)//4; enumeration runs only if m<=18; for 19<=m<=25 p=[1,0,..] so Z=1. I ran the repo's ml.compute_topological_indices against my own frontier-memoised matching counter (skeptic/t_idx.py). Results: aspirin (13 bonds) 335 vs 335, correct; donepezil 264 vs 965,380; imatinib 452 vs 79,015,504; n-icosane path (19 bonds) 1 vs 10,946 = F(21); C27 path 189 vs 317,811. On 2,148 single-fragment ChEMBL_37 max_phase=4 small molecules (my own pull, skeptic/fetch.py): 76.6% have >18 bonds (523 in 19-25, 1,123 >25) and 534 get Z=1. The expert said 73%; the difference is the denominator. The fix is cheap: my memoised DP gives imatinib's exact Z instantly. Hosoya is listed under distance-based at main.tex:114, so the misclassification claim is also upheld.

verdicts.item: graph-theory: SS_ABC, SS_AZ, SS_ABS and RABC have an extra product term in the numerator
verdicts.reproduction: ml.py:501-503 uses sqrt((xs+xy-2)/xy), (xy/(xs+xy-2))^3 and sqrt((xs+xy-2)/xs); ml.py:246 has num_rabc = rsuv + rpruv - 2. Block-1 ABC (ml.py:186) uses the correct (u+v-2)/uv, so the code is internally inconsistent. Aspirin: SS_ABC is 15.0236 in code vs 7.5058 for ABC4; SS_ABS is 23.330 vs 11.550. Both match the expert to 2 dp. Caveat: the source script degreessum_computation.py is not in the repo, so I cannot rule out that the group intended a variant. Ask them before 'fixing' it.

verdicts.item: graph-theory: reverse-degree block uses n+1-d(v), not Δ-d(v)+1, and reduces to size polynomials
verdicts.reproduction: ml.py:225 has rev_deg=[n+1-d]; aspirin RM1 = 1880 (rd in {11,12,13}). The identities hold exactly on my 2,148 molecules: RM1 = n(n+1)^2-4m(n+1)+M1 (residual 0) and RM2 = m(n+1)^2-(n+1)M1+M2 (residual 0). The draft now flags the mismatch itself at main.tex:111 (\todo 'v0.x code uses n+1-d(v) ... reconcile in M3'), so the paper/code contradiction is acknowledged but unresolved. I did not independently check the Kulli edge-sum vs vertex-sum point.

verdicts.item: graph-theory: Balaban J wrong for multi-fragment / salt graphs
verdicts.reproduction: ml.py:324 cyclo=m_bonds-n+2. metformin = 3.377 vs metformin·HCl = 0.0 (repo code). In my pull of 3,311 phase-4 records (salts included as separate records), 1,163 are multi-fragment and 169 of those get J=0. The expert's 474/1,959 used a different denominator. Same mechanism.

verdicts.item: graph-theory: R_k family drops edges / k>Δ ill-defined / R1_sigma ≡ sigma
verdicts.reproduction: ml.py:70-76 and 527-530. Molecules with at least one dropped edge, out of 2,148: k=1 0, k=2 6, k=3 18, k=4 1,173 (54.6%, matches the expert's 55%). By hand for Δ=3: k=2 maps d=1,2,3 to 1,3,2 and k=4 maps d=1 to 0. R1_sigma==sigma is numerically identical on all molecules and follows algebraically because R1 = Δ-d+1. The cited sources resolve on Crossref: Arockiaraj, Greeni, Kalaam, IJQC 2023 doi:10.1002/qua.27136, and Kalaam, Greeni, Arockiaraj, Front Chem 2024 doi:10.3389/fchem.2024.1470231. I did not re-read their exact R_k definition.

verdicts.item: graph-theory: exact duplicates and linear identities inflate 135 to ~115-127 distinct
verdicts.reproduction: allclose on 2,148 molecules found exactly 8 duplicate pairs: M2=SS_A, H=DSH, GA=DSGA, SC=DSR, DS1=DS2, W=W_v, Sz=Sz_v, sigma=R1_sigma. Identities with residual 0 or about 1e-15: BM=M1+M2, sigma=F-2M2, SS_M1=2M2, A=M1/2, TMA=2M1-2ISI, SS_TM=SS_HM-SS_M2. All also follow algebraically from ml.py.

verdicts.item: graph-theory: index matrix is mostly size (5 PCs explain 95%)
verdicts.reproduction: Independent set of N=2,148: 78 indices have |Spearman| >0.95 with heavy-atom count (99 have >0.9). Standardised PCA needs 3/5/9 components for 90/95/99% (expert: 3/5/10). Greedy grouping at |ρ|>0.99 gives 34 groups (expert: 37). Numerical rank of the standardised matrix on a random n=160 subset is 57 (expert: 61).

verdicts.item: qspr-ml: shared uncloned LinearRegression corrupts stored best models
verdicts.reproduction: Mechanism reproduced (skeptic/bug.py, real ml.py). With MODELS_AND_GRIDS restricted to LinearReg, best_models['MolWt'] and ['LogP'] share one estimator object, and the stored 'MolWt' model's predictions correlate 0.854 with LogP and 0.503 with MolWt. Severity is overstated, though. In the full 10-model run (n=160, p=135), LinearReg's CV R² is -1.2e9 (MolWt) and -1.5e10 (LogP), so it never wins. The stored best models were Lasso and ElasticNet and were not corrupted. The bug matters only if LinearReg wins, which is plausible only when n>>p. Side effect nobody flagged: R² values around -1e9 are written into the results table and UI.

verdicts.item: qspr-ml: indices element- and bond-order-blind; polarity targets not identifiable
verdicts.reproduction: Repo code gives identical values for all 135 indices for hexane, 1-pentanol, pentylamine and 1,4-butanediol, and again for cyclohexane, piperidine and tetrahydropyran (skeptic/t_idx.py).

verdicts.item: qspr-ml: indices add ~nothing beyond size for MolWt/MolMR; small gains for LogP/TPSA
verdicts.reproduction: Direction upheld, but the magnitude depends on n. Ridge (RidgeCV), 5x2 repeated CV, on 800 single-fragment approved drugs with MW<1000 (size / composition / TI / TI+comp): LogP 0.236 / 0.857 / 0.379 / 0.864; TPSA 0.427 / 0.920 / 0.593 / 0.928; MolMR 0.967 / 0.998 / 0.973 / 0.998. The TI gain over size is +0.14 (LogP) and +0.17 (TPSA) at n=800, against +0.05/+0.07 at n=154. That is not 'small', but it is dwarfed by element counts, and TI+comp ≈ comp.

verdicts.item: qspr-ml: single fixed split + heavy-tailed y makes R² unstable
verdicts.reproduction: Confirmed by reading: KFold(random_state=42) is created once per property (ml.py:822, RANDOM_STATE=42 in config.py:14). Not reproduced: the -66.8 Ridge TPSA result with peptides.

verdicts.reproduction: ml.py:719-733 caps at 999 when R²≥0.9999. Numerical rank is 57 at n=160 on my set, so most auxiliary regressions are perfect fits. I did not re-count 132/135.

verdicts.item: qspr-ml: uncorrected, rounded p-values on dependent tests
verdicts.reproduction: Y-scrambling on 160 approved drugs, Crippen LogP, 50 permutations, 135 Pearson tests each: mean 5.3 'significant' (nominal 6.75), median 0, max 94. 34% of permutations had ≥1 hit. Real LogP gives 127/135 significant. False positives arrive in collinear blocks. Rounding to 4 dp, NaN→r=0/p=1 and joint dropna confirmed by reading ml.py:672,698-702.

verdicts.item: software-eng: live site cannot start a first-time analysis (/validate 105-221 s vs 15 s abort)
verdicts.reproduction: The mechanism is real: index.html:450 sets AbortSignal.timeout(15000), and the probe pages at client MAX_LIMIT=20. Locally the probe took 15.1 s (asthma) and 37.7 s (hypertension); live /validate for glaucoma took 43.6 s cold. But the second call to live /validate took 0.52 s, because the chembl client's HTTP cache was warmed by the server-side call that kept running. So the UI's 'wait ~30s and try again' path does work. The claim 'cannot start' is overstated: first attempts for new diseases fail with a misleading message. I could not reproduce the 105-221 s timings.

verdicts.item: software-eng: silent failure handling; PubChem failures cached as {} permanently poison the cache
verdicts.reproduction: Partly refuted. fillna(0) and survival of ions are upheld: [Na+].[Cl-] survives with nonzero Z=1, RM1=18 and RF=54, so it is not 'everything else 0'. Bare excepts are confirmed in fetcher.py and main.py. But the 'poisoned cache' claim is false: fetcher.py:240-242 checks `if cached:`, and an empty {} (or empty list) is falsy, so a cached failure is re-fetched on the next run. The bioactivity cache stores an all-None dict, which is truthy, only on a successful empty query, not on exception (fetcher.py:493 returns without caching).

conflicts_between_experts: ChemGraphX citation: landscape-2026 says refs.bib has 19 entries and does not cite ChemGraphX; redteam-strategy says refs.bib:128 cites it and main.tex:70 positions it. Resolved: the draft was edited at 16:38 on 2026-10-02 and now has 24 entries including ChemGraphX and DOPtools. The landscape finding is stale. Several experts' main.tex line numbers are also off by about 3.

SoftwareX word limit: redteam-paper says about 3,000; redteam-strategy says 4,000. Secondary sources (search snippets of the SoftwareX guide) say 4,000, excluding title, authors, references and metadata tables. The primary page returned 403, so this needs manual confirmation.

Value of the indices over size: redteam-strategy says TI-135 is worse than 2 size counts on ESOL; qspr-ml says gains are small (+0.05/+0.07). My runs show both claims depend on the learner and on n. ESOL: Ridge TI 0.20 < size 0.34, but RF TI 0.53 > size 0.40. Approved drugs at n=800: TI beats size by +0.14 (LogP) and +0.17 (TPSA). The robust statement is that composition counts beat TI by a wide margin in every setting.

qspr-ml rates the shared LinearRegression bug as corrupting best models. In a realistic run LinearReg scores R² ≈ -1e9 (n<p) and never wins, so the stored models are unaffected. The mechanism is real; the practical severity is low.

software-eng: /validate takes 105-221 s and a first analysis 'cannot start'. My measurements: 15-44 s cold, and 0.5 s on retry because the chembl client's HTTP cache is warm, so the UI's retry message works.
software-eng: PubChem failures cached as {} 'poison the cache permanently'. The code's `if cached:` treats {} as a miss, so this is refuted.

Hosoya prevalence: 73% (graph-theory, N=1,959) vs 76.6% (mine, N=2,148), from different de-duplication. Multi-fragment counts: 474/1,959 vs 1,163/3,311 (mine includes salt records). Same conclusion either way.
C2 and C10 verdicts: the experts agree with each other but partly refute the lead (no 'all cancers' pull; family labels wrong). The whitelist zero-row count is 17 (curation) vs 18 (software-eng).
ChemGraphX size: landscape says 150 indices; the paper's own table sums to 149 (52+52+24+21) while its text says 150.
Kara et al. 2025 HAC R²: strategy quotes 0.998, which is the cubic model; the linear model is 0.999.
missing_coverage: Data licensing: ChEMBL is CC BY-SA 3.0. Redistributing drug sets, cached ChEMBL-derived files or result workbooks needs attribution and share-alike, and that must be stated in the paper and README alongside the MIT code licence. Nobody covered this.

Provenance of the non-standard formulas: SS_ABC/AZ/ABS, RABC, ABC_SC (ml.py:302, sqrt((s-2)/p)/sqrt(s), an unexplained hybrid) and n+1-d come from scripts that are not in the repo (degreessum_computation.py, degree_reverse_computation*.py, ml.py:4-6). Before 'fixing' them, get those scripts and the intended definitions from the Arockiaraj group. Some may be deliberate variants used in the group's published papers.

Feasibility of the Hosoya fix: exact Z is #P-hard in general. A frontier-memoised DP handled imatinib (41 bonds, Z ≈ 7.9e7) instantly, but nobody tested peptides and macrocycles (hundreds of bonds) or set a size cap / applicability rule.

Statistical numbers shown to users: the results table currently displays LinearReg R² around -1e9 (n<p), and UI 'best R²' values come from a single seed. Nobody specified what the UI should display (e.g. a ladder table with CIs over repeated CV).

Hidden state from the chembl_webresource_client HTTP cache (on-disk, with expiry) affects both the timing and the reproducibility of queries, separately from the app's own md5 cache. Nobody covered it.

Security and abuse beyond max_drugs: no auth or rate limit on /run, 8-hex-char job IDs, and CORS_ORIGINS values in config.py not inspected. Path traversal is not possible (canonical whitelist name), but nobody verified this explicitly.

Whether the planned ChemGraphX cross-check (main.tex:70 \todo M3) is feasible: ChemGraphX takes .mol/.pdb/adjacency, and the overlapping indices and naming conventions (e.g. its degree-sum indices) were never mapped against TopoQSPR's 135.
